blockers.quote: You could stop it here. Keep a few thousand, send the rest to Theo every night.
blockers.why: Check #5 But / therefore fails. This workable cap, followed immediately by the known debt-destruction route, removes the cause of every later escalation; day thirty-one through day forty-nine become “and then” beats sustained only by inaction.
blockers.fix: Remove the easy cap, or rebuild days twenty-seven to forty-nine so every delay is caused. Concretely: move Nana’s loss and the failed-giving attempt to day forty-eight, show you repeatedly choosing “one more night,” and begin the payoff immediately when that belief breaks.

blockers.quote: One grain of rice doubles across a chessboard chalked on Mrs. Vance's counter; at square thirteen it fills a coffee cup, and from square thirty-three the rice buries the kiosk, the pier, the ships in the bay and the city behind it.
blockers.why: Check #8 A picture only this premise can show fails. The chessboard is a generic exponential-growth illustration; rice could visualize bacteria, population or any doubling premise.
blockers.fix: Replace the > SCENE: with the money-specific image already latent in the outline: the balance flaps extend over the unchanged pier while Mrs. Vance rewrites one coffee’s price, closes the tab book, and Nana’s fixed bundle buys visibly less.

blockers.quote: A normal person with half a million buys a flat; you, by the time the agent calls back, could buy the building.
blockers.why: Check #7 Misconception first fails. The next beat says you believe day thirty-one might only just cover a flat, although this line has already established that an earlier balance buys the whole building. The acted-on wrong belief is internally impossible.
blockers.fix: Replace the flat action with a larger commitment: “You sign a non-refundable option on the whole pier, convinced day thirty-one might just cover it.” Then let Theo’s single billion-dollar result break that estimate.

suggestions.quote: The choice is morally live: three billion strangers' debts erased without anyone asking, and Mrs. Vance said no, and you keep that.
suggestions.fix: Owner suggestion: make respect for consent visibly compete with stopping the damage—show one borrower refusing before Mrs. Vance changes her own mind—so the dilemma has two defensible values rather than one clearly correct route.

suggestions.quote: Keep going and on day two hundred and sixty-seven there are more dollars than atoms in the observable universe (about 10^80).
suggestions.fix: Either cut this drive-by future fact or make it the final projected consequence of refusing the choice; presently the debt deadline, overflow, hyperinflation and atoms compete for the same beat.

suggestions.quote: the first batch is rejected, Mr. Halloran repairs the account map, and Theo runs it again.
suggestions.fix: Make the rejection force your decision rather than Halloran’s technical repair—for example, there is time for either the smallest debts or the locally verified debts, and you choose before Theo reruns the file.

keep.quote: Not when it's new. Your double is her half.
